lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Something's wrong.
lines.monologue: She said it before they reached the market gate. The sound was off — not the noise of trade, but the noise of its absence. Too few voices. Too many closed shutters.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: Half the stalls are shuttered. The ones still open are understocked. The dye merchant from before is gone entirely. Guard posts that were empty last time are manned now. Two at each entrance. They're not checking for weapons — they're counting heads.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: The fishing boats are in. All of them. It's midday.
lines.monologue: She counted the moorings. Every slip occupied. Nobody was out on the water. In a port town, that means either a storm nobody else can see or something worse.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: The grain exchange shut down. Three days ago, from the look of it. When the grain exchange closes, everything downstream collapses. Bakeries. Feed suppliers. Livestock pricing. It's not one failure — it's a cascade.
lines.monologue: She was reading the empty stalls the way Lex reads inscriptions. Each absence was a word in a sentence she didn't want to finish.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.text: Why would the grain exchange close?

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: It wouldn't. Not for weather. Not for politics. Not for anything I know about. The exchange is the spine of Solenne's economy. Shutting it down is like stopping your own heart to fix a headache.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: Unless the supply lines feeding it already stopped.
lines.monologue: She said it flatly. Not speculation — trajectory. Following the logistics backward to the only conclusion that fit.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: The eastern road brings grain from the Valdrihn lowlands. The river route brings it from the Ereivyn border farms. If both stopped at the same time, that's not banditry. Bandits hit one route. Two simultaneous failures means the source dried up.
lines.monologue: She pulled a map from her pack. Unfolded it on a barrel top. Traced the routes with her finger. The lines converged through a valley they'd passed three weeks ago. The one where the grass leaned east.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: The merchant I know — Dalla. She runs the secondary textile exchange. If anyone has the full picture, she will.
lines.monologue: She was already moving. Not panicked. Purposeful. The way she moves when the numbers matter and the margin for error is shrinking.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.monologue: Dalla looked older. Not from time — from worry. The kind that sits in the shoulders and doesn't leave.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Dalla says the caravans aren't being attacked. They're turning back. The drivers say the roads feel wrong. Animals refuse to go forward. The mules stop and won't be led.
lines.monologue: She relayed it carefully. Not embellishing. Not softening. Dalla's words, not hers.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: The same phenomenon. The surveyor reports described animals avoiding the affected areas. Horses especially.
lines.monologue: He was connecting it. Not guessing — placing the pieces next to each other and watching the shape they made.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: So the distortion zones are spreading. And they're cutting across trade infrastructure.
lines.monologue: She looked at the map again. Drew her finger along the blocked routes. Then along the distortion site they'd marked two days ago. The geometry was obvious. The affected area was growing.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: If I map the blocked routes against the distortion we found, the dead zone extends roughly forty kilometers along the eastern valley. That's not a ruin being strange. That's a region being rewritten.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: It's not just the land.
lines.monologue: He felt it. Not through his headache — through his feet. The ground in Solenne felt thinner than it had last time. Not unstable. Just... less certain. As if the world here had started doubting its own foundations.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: If the eastern routes stay closed for another week, Solenne loses the ability to feed itself through winter. That's not a market adjustment. That's a famine.
lines.monologue: She said 'famine' the way she says everything important. Quietly. Without drama. The weight of the word doing its own work.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: This isn't ruins being corrupted. This is the corruption using the ruins as a starting point and growing outward. The infrastructure — roads, trade, agriculture — it's all downstream of the same cause.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: Then we need to understand the cause. Because the effect is going to reach everywhere eventually.
lines.monologue: She folded the map. Not carefully — urgently. The first time any of them had seen her handle her supplies with anything other than precision.

choices.text: People first. Help Solenne survive the week.
The source. If we don't stop it, helping here just delays the collapse.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.text: People first. Solenne needs supply lines reopened before we chase the cause.
lines.lens: Immediate threat: starvation timeline is seven days. Investigation timeline: unknown. Triage says address the certain harm before the uncertain one.
lines.monologue: I can't save everyone from something I don't understand yet. But I can keep people fed for another week. That's enough. It has to be enough.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: I can reroute through the southern pass. It adds two days to the grain run but it avoids the dead zone entirely.
lines.monologue: She was already unfolding the map again. The urgency was still there, but it had a shape now. A problem she could solve with rope and distance and knowing which trails were still good.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: I'll talk to Dalla. If we can get even partial shipments moving, the market stabilizes enough to buy time.
lines.monologue: Time. That was the real currency here. Not grain, not coin. Time before the thing none of them understood finished rewriting the ground beneath them.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.text: The source. If we don't stop whatever's causing this, Solenne starves anyway — just slower.
lines.lens: Strategic assessment: treating symptoms extends the timeline but doesn't change the outcome. The dead zone is expanding. Every day we spend on relief, the problem grows.
lines.monologue: It's the harder call. People will go hungry while we chase something we can't name. But the alternative is coming back to a town that's already gone.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: Then we move fast. I'll leave supply notes with Dalla — alternate routes, cache locations, contingency stores. It's not a solution but it's a bandage.
lines.monologue: She didn't argue. She prepared. That's how Rynn disagrees — by making sure the plan she doesn't love still has the best chance of working.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I can feel where it's strongest. East. Whatever's there, it's not hiding.
lines.monologue: He said it quietly. The ground under his feet hummed and he listened to it the way you listen to someone telling you something they need you to hear.
